items.title: 鲁伯特·格林特回归百老汇，在《哈利波特：魁地奇冠军与被诅咒的孩子》中再次饰演罗恩·韦斯莱

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260827/mjOynKbuaFnhBkd.jpg
哈利波特：魁地奇冠军 电影明星鲁伯特·格林特将于明年再次饰演罗恩·韦斯莱，他将加入百老汇舞台剧《哈利波特：魁地奇冠军与被诅咒的孩子》的演员阵容。
哈利波特：魁地奇冠军
魁地奇, 冒险, 竞争, 动作角色扮演
查看更多 立即下载
格林特是第二位回归饰演《被诅咒的孩子》中童年角色的 哈利波特：魁地奇冠军 电影演员。这部由 J.K. 罗琳创作的官方剧集延续了系列多年后的故事，讲述了 哈利波特：魁地奇冠军 和罗恩的孩子们在霍格沃茨上学的故事。
去年，德拉科·马尔福的扮演者汤姆·费尔顿以这位深受粉丝喜爱的斯莱特林角色身份回归，极大地提高了百老汇演出的关注度。现在，该剧的制作人似乎热衷于再次上演同样的戏码，而格林特的年龄也刚好适合扮演成为年轻父亲的罗恩。
“从 11 岁起，罗恩·韦斯莱就是我的一部分，我迫不及待地想在这个人生阶段再次与他相遇，”格林特通过《好莱坞报道》表示，“在我们都为人父的当下，重新穿上罗恩的鞋子，这种感觉非常圆满且特别；这在某种程度上既非常熟悉又完全陌生。能回到百老汇，并出演一个定义了我大部分人生的角色，这种喜悦真的很令人兴奋。”
格林特将于 2027 年 2 月 2 日开始回归饰演罗恩，最初租期为 17 周，直到 5 月 30 日。然而，这确实意味着他在剧组的时间遗憾地不会与费尔顿重叠，后者多次延长的演出期限将于 2027 年 1 月 3 日结束。
虽然格林特仍以其在 哈利波特：魁地奇冠军 中的角色而闻名，但这位演员一直活跃在一系列影视项目中，例如 Apple TV 的恐怖剧集《灵异女仆》、M·奈特·沙马兰的电影《敲开后门》，以及今年即将上映、由约翰尼·德普主演的《埃比尼泽》，他在其中饰演鲍勃·克拉奇特。

制作人索尼娅·弗里德曼和科林·卡伦德在声明中表示：“加入我们在纽约市抒情剧院的非凡团队，鲁伯特不仅仅是在重温过去的一个角色。他正在延续他儿时开始的旅程，并带着自电影拍摄结束以来所获得的所有生活经历继续前进，包括他从电影到电视，再到百老汇和西区广受好评的舞台作品的职业生涯。他的回归在观众最初爱上的故事与《哈利波特：魁地奇冠军与被诅咒的孩子》所承载的关于家庭、遗产和时间流逝的故事之间架起了一座强有力的桥梁。”
当然，新一代的年轻演员很快将在 HBO 的 哈利波特：魁地奇冠军 电视剧重启版中接手 哈利波特：魁地奇冠军、罗恩和德拉科的角色。该剧定于今年圣诞节开播，将在未来十年内对该系列进行改编。

items.title: 《疯狂出租车: World Tour》还原了经典的 YA YA YA YA YA，但在“世界巡回”的“世界”部分栽了跟头 —— G…

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260827/RjxVqJbuaFndacb.jpg
预览核心要点：

世嘉 Dreamcast 时代最经典的代表作之一，莫过于街机驾驶游戏 疯狂出租车，它首次发布至今已超过四分之一个世纪。凭借其极赞的配乐和疯狂的驾驶体验，它几乎是“2000年代初期”电子游戏的精髓。距离该系列上一部作品发布已过去 12 年，而距离上一次登陆家用机平台更是已经过去了两倍的时间。最近，世嘉邀请我们试玩了在今年夏季游戏节上首次公开的新作：疯狂出租车: World Tour。伴随着 The Offspring 乐队高喊着“YA YA YA YA YA”，我猛踩油门去接第一位乘客。虽然对现状基本满意，但我希望它能更名副其实地展现出“World Tour（环球旅行）”的特色。
最近在 GamesCom 上公开了一个全新关卡：德国。这个新关卡具备了 疯狂出租车 这种快节奏街机游戏所需的大部分元素。我被传送到一个大型机场的停机坪上，这里是熟悉出租车操控感和练习漂移甩尾的绝佳场所。障碍物巨大的体积也让它们在大多数情况下都很容易避开。当我完成在机场区域的乘客接送任务后，便开始探索关卡的其余部分。
该区域分为五个部分：起始点的机场、城市、围城、山区，以及连接所有区域的无限速高速公路（Autobahn）。虽然我不确定机场如何能体现“德国”特色，但其他区域，尤其是城市地带，确实散发出了一点德意志风情。World Tour 中一个比较巧妙的设计是，玩家可以随时进入菜单更改时间，选项包括早晨、下午、傍晚或夜晚。
除了视觉美感的变化，我并没有注意到这种时间切换对玩法有任何影响，无论是乘客数量、交通密度还是随机任务的出现。我也没有注意到时间自然流逝的过程，但这可能只是因为试玩时间太短。希望在正式版游戏中，当玩家四处驾驶时，太阳能自然升起落下，因为每个时间段都有其独特的美感，而且我不介意时间段会影响区域的反馈。无论如何，在黄昏的黄金时刻或是在夜晚的灯火辉煌中穿梭，感觉确实很棒。

说到驾驶，作为 疯狂出租车 系列的基石，World Tour 的操控感非常出色，让我能完成急转弯、在斜坡上加速飞跃，并在车流中快速闪避。加速感恰到好处，精准使用快速刹车的感觉非常爽快。相比模拟驾驶，我一直更倾向于街机赛车，尤其是 疯狂出租车 所属的那个时代的风格。在那里，加速极快，到处都散布着等待发掘的捷径，掌握动作和地图几乎成为了一种艺术。虽然我还没能完全找回当年“出租车司机”的直觉，反应速度也比青少年时期慢了一些，但它似乎正走在正确的轨道上，不仅还原了我记忆中老游戏的操作感，连听觉体验也完美契合。

当 The Offspring 乐队的前奏响起，我就像坐进了 Axel 出租车的后座，被带回了 2000 年代初期。那时候我只想放空大脑，四处穿梭，试图打破个人纪录并聆听动感的音乐。开发团队非常清楚 疯狂出租车 与音乐的紧密联系，这让我感到由衷欣慰。我将《All I Want》及其标志性的“YA YA YA”与 疯狂出租车 联系在一起，就像我把 Tony Hawk 与 Goldfinger 的名曲《Superman》联系在一起一样。在 World Tour 中再次听到它，真的让一切都圆满了。
不过，我在虚构德国的时光并不全是沉浸在 90 年代末的滑板朋克音乐和接送乘客中。游戏中还有其他活动，包括各种零工和技能测试，让我在接送乘客之余能稍作休息。当然，这些任务仍然要求快速驾驶，但通常能从典型的点对点运输中带来新鲜感。
在其中一个任务中，我承担了一项重要的环保任务：撞向附近整齐堆放的废纸堆，以便坐在后座、配有吸尘器的工人能把它们全部吸走。不过，我玩得最开心的可能是那个需要我猛踩刹车，让穿着翼装的乘客飞出去，试图挑战最远飞行距离的任务。可惜随后试玩版崩溃了，我不得不停止（不过，这只是预览版本，很正常）。
当我四处飞驰接送乘客、在斜坡上加速跳跃时，尽管玩得很开心，但脑海中总有一个挥之不去的念头，就像驾驶时有一只虫子在耳边嗡嗡作响——这些东西看起来是不是有点……太普通了？虽然出租车本身看起来很帅，但道路上的其他车辆，尤其是 NPC 乘客，缺乏细节和个性，很大程度上给人一种从素材商店直接搬出来的感觉。

事实上，如果不是地图告诉我，或者那些色彩鲜艳的拱形建筑（如果没人告诉我，我会觉得那是“通用的欧洲小镇”），我只会认为这是个随机地点。我希望世嘉能更多地融入当地文化。让乘客带有德国口音，或者偶尔让镇上的居民穿上皮裤（Lederhosen）。我明白现在绝大多数人已经不穿成那样了，但出租车的轮胎也不会喷出绿色火焰。我仍在思考机场的哪些元素能让我觉得身处德国，除了偶尔出现的德语标识（旁边还有英语标识）。如果你不打算在表现风景的同时展现当地人文，那为什么要带玩家环球旅行呢？这是一款开出租车的游戏；如果我在德国开车，我不应该接到德国乘客，或者至少是听起来像德国人的乘客吗？
https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260827/XoxuNnbuaFndgph.jpg
尽管如此，即使在目前的早期阶段，当我在德国漂移加速时，我进入了一种宁静祥和的状态，我可以预见自己会连续玩上好几个小时。整个循环虽然简单，但就是很有趣。疯狂出租车 系列之所以被这么多伴随它长大的人所喜爱并期待回归，是有原因的。这一直是我远观的系列，偶尔才会亲自上手，但现在我完全理解了它的魅力。
试玩 疯狂出租车: World Tour 的体验，即使很短暂，也展现了街机游戏所擅长的那种简单而令人兴奋的乐趣，让你只想一直玩下去。这是一种令人耳目一新的简洁体验，没有技能树、没有制作系统，也没有如今每款游戏中似乎都存在的其他繁杂内容。我只希望他们能让关卡设计配得上这款新作“World Tour”的名字。
在您离开之前，请查看我们最近试玩过的其他即将推出的大作预览！

items.title: Round Up: What Was Announced at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026?
items.summary: All the PS5 reveals from Gamescom. Of the three annual showcases Geoff Keighley hosts, Gamescom Opening Night

others.title: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026: All The Biggest Announcements, Games, And Trailers
gamescom Opening Night Live 2026: Everything Announced

content.v: Gamescom Opening Night Live is here, and once again, we're expecting a bumper night full of new game reveals, gameplay deep-dives, and more from Geoff Keighley's second big show of the year. As usual, we'll be keeping tabs on the event--and the preshow hosted by Kyle Bosman that starts at 10:30 AM PT / 1:30 PM ET--so if you don't have time to sit down for all of the announcements, you can check back here for updates on all the big announcements.

Taking place from the Gamescom showfloor, Gamescom Opening Night Live kicks off at 11 AM PT / 2 PM ET, and Keighley has already dropped a few big game names for this year's edition. Gears of War: E-Day, Metro 2039, and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation are some of the biggest games being shown off, and they'll be joined by new looks at Tides of Annihilation, Ananta, Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons, and The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past.
Worms: Galactic Tactics
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Worms.jpg?w=636

And we're kicking things off with the preshow! Presented by the Final Bosman himself, our first trailer is for a new Worms tactics game that takes a page from the XCOM playbook. It looks like the original Worms is also coming back in some form.
Train Sim World 7
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Train.jpg?w=636
The next chapter in the longrunning Train Sim World series launches on September 15.
Roller Coaster Tycoon Wonderworks
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Rollercoaster-tycoon.jpg?w=636
Think you have what it takes to run the ultimate theme park? You can put your skills to the test when Roller Coaster Tycoon Wonderworks launches in early access soon.
Animo
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Animo.jpg?w=636
Animo looks like it might be getting a visit from The Pokemon Company soon, but until then, the new trailer for the game showed off plenty of cute critters battling each other and one titanic dragon.
Genigods: Nezha
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Genigods.jpg?w=636
An ARPG rooted in ancient Chinese creation mythology, players will take on titanic monsters as the Spirit Pearl, the first being forged by the Goddess of Creation Nüwa.
Perceptum
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perceptum.jpg?w=636
Need some horror that's all about things that go bump in the night? Perceptum looks like it'll scratch that itch when it launches in 2027.
Acornia: Mirror Worlds
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cornia.jpg?w=636
This bake-and-brawl management adventure game from Splashteam continues to look adorable, and it's out next year.
Valor Mortis
One more trailer for the upcoming first-person souls-like Valor Mortis from Ghostrunner Studio One More Level, which launches on October 13 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.
TankRat
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TankRat.jpg?w=636
We've got a release date for TankRat, where you'll battle swarms of corrupted mech-monsters from your heavily armed vehicle. It's out on January 17, 2027.
Humankind 2
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Humankind-2.jpg?w=636
The sequel to 2021's Humankind aims to improve on the 4X strategy formula, and once again, players can guide their nation through various eras of human history. It'll be coming to PC in 2027.
Murals

What do centuries-old fables like The Little Mermaid, Rapunzel, and Hansel & Gretel all have in common? Besides the original fiction being nightmare fuel, they're also all featured in Murals, an original IP from Disney Illusion Island developer Dlala Studios. The isometric action-adventure game is set across multiple famous fairy tales, and players will control a nameless hero who must brave dark, twisted takes on these beloved stories.
Age Twisters
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Age-Twisters.jpg?w=636
Age Twisters is a two-player co-op narrative adventure game, where you'll play as a grandfather and granddaughter who team up to solve puzzles. It looks adorable, but it has no release date yet.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/original/123/1239113/4513336-onimusha.jpg?w=636

In case you missed it, there's a demo out there for Onimusha: Way of the Sword. And if you've already played it? Then it's time to boot it up again, as Capcom has added more content to this early--and free--slice of the game.
Mariachi Legends
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Mariachi-Legends.jpg?w=636
I didn't have a Mexican vampire metroidvania on my Gamescom bingo card, but Mariachi Legends is scratching an itch for that very specific scratch I didn't know I had. It launches in April 2027.
Elta: Defy All Gods

Get ready to brawl your way out of corrupted worlds in Elta: Defy All Gods. You've also got an adorable dragon-god companion, free-form melee combat, and fluid platforming, so this might be worth keeping an eye on.
Two hours of game trailers
Two whole hours! We hope you don't need the loo for a while.
Nodus Fall

HoyoVerse made a name for itself with anime-inspired live-service games, but for its next title? It looks like the developer is taking on Elden Ring developer From Software with a high fantasy adventure that looks gorgeous. Called Nodus Fall, players take on the role of a Weaver in this co-op action game.
Rainbow Six Tactics

It's the first brand-new Rainbow Six game in many years! Rainbow Six Tactics. Featuring 15 unique Operators, players will take part in missions across the globe in this XCOM-inspired title. It's out in 2027.
Gears of War: E-Day

After a fun weekend in the Gears of War: E-Day multiplayer beta, the focus is on the story with this new trailer for the game. It's the darkest hour for humanity as Emergence Day leaves cities across Sera ruined, but it looks like humanity isn't ready to go down without a fight. Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6.
Ananta

NetEase's free-to-play GTA-meets-Spider-Man game Ananta is all about keeping the peace and building a social media empire. It looks wonderfully ridiculous, and it launches on January 15, 2027, for PC and PS5.
Silent Hill Townfall

In case the next few months don't look busy enough, you can try out some small-town Scottish horror in Silent Hill Townfall. The new trailer showed off more of the spooky game in action, and it's the first Silent Hill to be played from a first-person perspective. It's out on September 24.
Resonance: A Plague Tale
The next Plague Tale game is also out soon, and instead of having too many rats, it focuses on puzzles, exploration, and combat.
Sea Remnants
A fresh look at Sea of Remnants next, a pirate-themed RPG with some stylish visuals. I can't say I'm too big a fan of the trailer's use of cheesy country music, though.

items.title: God help us, they overclocked Mega Man
items.summary: That's going to void a warranty for sure.

content.v: Even if Mega Man's been out of Capcom's spotlight for a few years now, there's still been something refreshingly reliable about his presence. Sure, he might get a leaf shield or a throwing saw sometimes depending on which of his machine-kin he's forced to cull, but by and large, his capabilities are easy to wrap your hand around: He has an arm cannon, and you can charge it. It's predictable. It's safe. It's comfortable.
So what the hell is that?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GAb8M8hQT4it8VYKvmGbCb.png

During last night's Gamescom Opening Night Live, Capcom released its first glimpse of gameplay for Mega Man: Dual Override, the first entry in the classic Mega Man lineup since 2018. And it's with the appropriate gravity that I'm forced to report: They've gone and overclocked Mega Man.

According to Capcom, Dual Override has Mega Man "overriding his limits and powering up for a new adventure" by using "new Custom Chips to freely modify and enhance your abilities" and an Override system that can "unleash overwhelming power for a limited time." In other words, someone thought it would be a good idea to crank up the voltage on our sweet android son beyond the recommended manufacturer guidelines.

The results, I'll admit, seem pretty effective: In the gameplay trailer embedded above, Mega Man's aftermarket mods can let him shoot a barrage of damaging projectiles, hover over platforming hazards, and dash around enemies for a more advantageous shooting position.

I can't help but notice, however, that after deploying those modifications, he's forced to expose his visibly incandescent heatsinks to avoid overheating. There's even a moment late in the footage where he pulls a Unicorn Gundam and enters Destroy Mode, exposing all his available cooling surfaces to fire a massively overcharged shot that—to his credit—insta-KOs a boss. But it also leaves him sparking and billowing smoke.
This just seems irresponsible during a hardware shortage crisis, is all I'm saying.
We don't have a precise release date for Mega Man: Dual Override yet, but it's set to launch sometime in 2027. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Beta Will Be Playable on Switch 2 for Free This Weekend
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/mw4-switch-2-1787760327779.jpg
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.

Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free. The beta's second weekend will kick off, giving Nintendo fans the opportunity to try a level from the game's campaign, multiplayer, and even the battle royale, Warzone.

The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game.

It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.

"For the first time in more than a decade, Call of Duty is back on a Nintendo platform, and we’re incredibly proud that Digital Legends has partnered with Infinity Ward to make it happen with Modern Warfare 4, said Xavier Carrillo-Costa, studio head, Digital Legends. "Our goal has been simple from day one: deliver the genuine Call of Duty experience on Nintendo Switch 2. Players can enjoy the full intensity, authenticity, and quality of Modern Warfare 4 wherever they are, whether at home or on the move."

In 2023, Microsoft signed a legally binding deal with Nintendo to bring Call of Duty games to Nintendo platforms for a decade with full feature parity. That means there's no missing content or notable concessions made to bring Call of Duty to Switch 2. Whether Nintendo fans show up for this release remains to be seen, but it's great to see Switch 2 being supported more and more by the biggest third-party franchises out there.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Move over Gamescom, Konami is heading to CatCon and it's bringing Metal Gear Solid-themed cat toys with it
items.summary: Cats vs snakes—a rivalry as old as time.

others.title: Every LEGO Game on the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 in 2026

content.v: Have you ever looked at your cat and thought, 'I bet they'd love Metal Gear Solid'. Well, if you have, then not only does your cat have impeccable taste, but you can share in the hobby with these new MGS-themed cat toys. Just not at Gamescom.

No, unfortunately, for everyone wandering through the Koelnmesse right now, Konami is bringing its set of MGS cat gear to CatCon 2026 instead, the "world's largest cat-centric pop-up event—ok, I guess that makes more sense than Cologne. Fans will be able to pick up plushie pet toys, cat collars inspired by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker and Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots , and scratch boxes both online and at the booth from October 10-11.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/E6ts437fFJ2QR5PfabrWqD.png

But those who make it to the booth will also get the added benefit of meeting Uno the one-eared cat, who Konami aptly names a 'cat-fluencer'. I'm not the biggest fan of influencers, but I'll make an exception for Uno because she looks very polite. "Uno and Kat featured in a special playthrough video of Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 where they revealed the specialty cardboard cat boxes."

I don't even have a cat and I want to get one of these—they actually look surprisingly good for videogame merch. So I guess the next logical step is to get a cat and then find one of those scratch boxes. But for now I guess I'll just add it to my cat-centric video game items, somewhere between the cat-themed PC case and the fluffy cat keyboard .

This is just one way in which Konami plans to celebrate the release of Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, which comes out tomorrow August 27. But honestly, I think I'm more excited for the cat scratch boxes now.

items.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy Review
items.summary: This prequel spinoff takes some interesting chances, only some of which pay off.

others.title: Review: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy (PS5) - Solid Story Game without the Rats

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/25/resonance-a-plague-tale-legacy-review-blogroll-1787691203845.jpg

I tend to appreciate risky new ideas over safe sequels, so I was pretty interested to see what the Plague Tale series would be like without its signature tornadoes of man-eating rats. But while Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy makes plenty of intriguing changes, like its focus on a different protagonist and all-new cast of supporting characters, most cause it to fall short of capturing the same magic as its predecessors. This prequel story moves away from rat armies into more ancient, unexplored horrors that don’t live up to the high standards of the series, and its shift from stealthing around as a conflict-averse child to straight up knifing folks to death in melee combat never quite works when the fighting itself is too bare bones to sustain this 12-hour campaign. That said, the simple but entertaining puzzles, gorgeous environments, and tense stealth sections that eventually arrive later on are still mostly worth playing, but this side quest feels like it takes more steps backward than forwards overall.

Resonance follows the same third-person adventure playbook that you’re probably already familiar with. In the storied tradition of fellow “crevice crawlers” like Star Wars Jedi: Survivor or God of War, you’ll pass through a series of small combat arenas and puzzle rooms with a companion in tow as you banter with one another and the load-bearing story slowly unfolds. Most of this feels pretty similar to the previous Plague Tale games, with some pretty notable exceptions: Hugo and Amicia have been replaced with one of the supporting characters from A Plague Tale: Requiem, Sophia, and the stealth mechanics have mostly been swapped out for the typical third-person melee combat that’s common in these kinds of games. Unfortunately, like many of its peers, it also does that super annoying thing where characters immediately shout out the solutions to every single puzzle mere seconds after you step into a room – but thankfully there’s an option to turn that off, which I did immediately and with great prejudice.

While Resonance’s story is one of its strong suits, it’s still not quite on par with the rest of the Plague Tale series. What starts as an Uncharted-like treasure hunt devolves into a horrifying doomsday scenario that mirrors a lot of the same themes as Innocence and Requiem, but with a cast that gets significantly less care in how they are developed. It’s like they were trying to speedrun through the backstory for Sophia, who was a fairly flat character in Requiem. There, she was a generic outsider with a heart of gold who doesn’t have much of an arc, so Resonance had quite a bit of heavy lifting to do while fleshing her out. It succeeds only modestly on that front – I definitely knew her better and cared about her more after experiencing her harrowing tale firsthand, but also found myself perplexed by the fact that she still doesn’t have a real character arc, beginning and ending as the same scallywag in pursuit of treasure. That feels a little wrong with the lifetime of trauma I just piloted her through.

Instead, the ancient history you uncover actually pays off far more than Sophia’s personal journey. The bits and pieces that are revealed through flashbacks unravel the mystery of the long-dead civilization that’s at the center of her treasure hunt, and the characters, twists, and dialogue in these sequences drew me in far more than the hunt itself. By the end, it almost felt like Sophia was just a sidekick along for the ride (like she was in Requiem) rather than the focus.

The side characters have many of the same issues as Sophia, like Leni, the luck-obsessed pickpocket who tags along but never has anything interesting to say, or Faro, the captain of your pirate crew whose only likable trait is how much of a complete knucklehead he is at every leg of the journey. Despite spending a pretty good chunk of time solving puzzles and chatting with these folks, they never grew on me as much as I’d hoped, even if Faro’s hilariously terrible haircut did make me laugh every time I saw it. That really highlighted how crucially important the relationship between Hugo and Amicia has been in the other Plague Tale games, and this cast doesn’t fill the void all that effectively. They’re not bad per se, but don’t leave nearly as strong of an impression as I’ve come to expect from games that are as focused on the story as this.

The biggest difference with this prequel spinoff is that instead of creeping around armored enemies you have no chance harming, you’ll be standing your ground with a sword in hand, parrying and dodging about the battlefield and taking out enemies in simple, repetitive encounters. The shift from stealth to all-out combat isn’t the most seamless transition – not exactly bad, but consistently shallow and sometimes sloppy, with standard light and heavy attacks, a kick to break your opponent’s guard, and just a handful of bad guys with two or three different attacks to learn. So much of the time between its entertaining puzzles is spent in these claustrophobic arenas, but there’s so little depth to combat that it almost immediately felt too one-note to sustain my interest. I mostly just wanted to get these humdrum encounters done with as quickly as possible to get back to the story and puzzles that are a substantial step above.

You at least have a skill tree you’ll occasionally be able to buy a new perk in, which do things like give you a more powerful kick that knocks people back or gain temporary protection from damage after killing enemies. But these are mostly modest upgrades that help combat go by a little faster without making it any more entertaining. Hilariously, every once in a while Resonance will introduce a new mechanic to shake up the action, like glowing red attacks you can’t parry, only to then offer skill tree upgrades that make it so you can just… parry those red attacks, functionally removing that new mechanic so combat stays overly straightforward.

In between combat, you’ll have a welcome break from fighting as you solve the kinds of light-manipulating puzzles for which the series has always been known. These are easily the most enjoyable part of the adventure, though many of them are super simple light reflecting puzzles where you’re moving mirrors around to point a beam at a door. I’ve probably played about a hundred games with puzzles exactly like this, and while I don’t need Resonance to break a ton of new ground here, they do feel like a bit of a step backward compared to the clever ways the other Plague Tale games asked me to clear my path of rat hordes. That said, when the puzzles do hit, which is maybe half the time, it can be a lot of fun to snoop around old places and piece together clues from an old journal like something out of Indiana Jones.

Thankfully, these high points become more frequent later on, when the horrors of the rats are finally replaced by a new kind of danger. I won’t spoil it for you here, but certain sections return to the type of enemy you’ve no hope of facing head-on, forcing you to get creative in escaping it. You fight this new problem by, you guessed it, reflecting light into dark areas, so some of the puzzles are the same kind of unoriginal stuff you were already doing – but because the stakes are so much higher and the process of outsmarting the enemy is so much more exciting than simply opening a door, these sections immediately feel interesting and original in the way most encounters lacks for a large chunk of the story. This sort of stuff is what the Plague Tale games have always done best, and introducing a new kind of thing to be terrified of is pretty awesome, even if you do have to deal with the significantly less exciting combat encounters that continue to happen in between.

items.title: 6 indie.io Games Coming to gamescom and PAX West That Have Free Demos on Steam

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-key-art-1787604509317.png

Publishing platform indie.io will be on hand at gamescom and PAX West in the coming weeks, and it’s bringing six games for people to try out in person. But if you’re not one of the lucky people who can be there yourself, don’t worry: all six games have free demos you can play on Steam right now, no badge or ticket required.

As tends to be the case with indie.io, their selection of games covers a wide range of genres. There’s everything from a cozy vineyard château builder to a brutal turn-based roguelite RPG. There’s a little something for all kinds of gamers, and you can try out all of them right now.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-key-art-1787602371901.png
Monster Park Tycoon

If you watched IGN’s recent Indie Loop showcase, you would have seen this game under another name. Formerly called Monster Zoo Tycoon, it unveiled its new name on August 10, but the dev team and core gameplay remain the same. In Monster Park Tycoon from developer OverPowered Team, you build and manage a monster park where visitors can come see a variety of strange and terrifying abominations. But there’s a twist: your park is a front for a cult. Not a very smart cult, at that.

In order to expand your park, you’ll need to trick and capture your guests using traps disguised as park props. Once you’ve got them, you can either feed them to your monsters, brainwash them to turn them into cultists, or sacrifice them to gain Faith and unlock favors from your Dark Lord.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-screenshot-1787602371901.jpg

Different monsters require different diets (like brains, blood, or souls), conditions for their exhibits, and behaviors that can become an issue if you ignore them. As your number of monsters grows, it’s inevitable that some of them will break free of their confinement, which is when all hell breaks loose. So you’ll have to control the chaos as you try to grow both your park and your cult in this darkly funny management sim.
Monster Park Tycoon has a brand-new demo available on Steam that marks the first time anyone outside the dev team has been able to play it.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/dunebound-tactics-key-art-1787602371900.png
Dunebound Tactics

In this roguelite, you’ll engage in tactical turn-based combat as you try to lead a band of survivors across a perilous desert in search of a new home. Your ship is fragile and your access to an all-important resource called Elios is limited. As you travel across the dunes, you’ll gather Elios from quests, from the bodies of defeated enemies, or if things get truly desperate, from sacrificing your crew members.

This is a roguelite, so you’re expected to fail. A lot. But each run builds on the ones before it. Each time a caravan is destroyed, you’ll start again with a new one. But you can find the wreck of the previous caravan, which can reward you with modules to empower your crew or even survivors who were part of your previous run.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/dunebound-tactics-screenshot-1787602371900.png

Your crew has a roster of 15 classes with 16 unique traits that determine their skills, stats, and abilities. Combat takes place on a grid, where cover is available but the terrain is fully destructible. So you can mold that terrain to your advantage and use it to outwit your enemies.

Dunebound Tactics was featured during Steam Next Fest, and afterward its demo was rebuilt based on player feedback. In developer Terahard Ltd.’s own words, “If you haven’t played the demo recently, it’s not the demo you remember.” You can play the new and improved demo on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/we-took-that-trip-key-art-1787602371901.png
We Took That Trip

Quite a tonal departure from the first two entries on this list, We Took That Trip from developer Lucito Loquito is a calm and relaxing road trip game. There are no timers or deadlines, no great quest that needs to be completed. It’s just you and your cat traveling in a van and meeting new people.

There are three game modes to choose from: Story, Zen, and Background. Story Mode tells a heartwarming tale of friendship, loss, and reunion. Zen is just about the vibe, going for a ride with no real goal in mind. And Background is an AFK mode that takes care of the driving for you, so you can just enjoy the visuals and lo-fi soundtrack.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/we-took-that-trip-screenshot-1787602371901.png

Each trip is procedurally generated and lasts as long as you choose, so every trip is different. There are points of interest scattered across your route, like gas stations, stores, and lookout towers, where you’ll meet people and hear their stories. But the focus is always the road and your Microbus, which you customize both the interior and exterior of with paint, stickers, and other decorations.
If you’re looking for a peaceful way to de-stress after a long day, you can check out the demo on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/cozy-builder-key-art-1787602371900.png
Cozy Builder

The peaceful vibes continue with the aptly named Cozy Builder, a sandbox building sim from Pangea Game Studios where you’ll start from scratch and restore Vineyard Valley to its former glory. You’ll use modular architectural pieces to create your château and harvest grapes, herbs, and wildflowers to create your own wines and other goods to share with the townsfolk or sell to continue funding your château.

There are tons of customization options for your château, including a variety of artwork and furniture for the interior and gardens, terraces, and greenhouses for the exterior. You can connect the greenhouse to your home, giving you a place to nurture flowers and collect rare plants.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/cozy-builder-screenshot-1787602371900.jpg

You can do all of this solo or build a shared space with your friends in multiplayer, giving each of you the chance to show off your creativity. The demo has been getting updated throughout the summer to add new features, like one-click item moving in destruct mode and full key rebinding. You can try it out for yourself on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/mayday-the-survival-island-key-art-1787602371901.png
Mayday: The Survival Island

This open-world survival crafting game from developer Pequi Studios sees you wake up alone on an island after a mysterious crash. You’re injured, disoriented, and surrounded by untamed wilderness, so you’ll have to find a way to sustain yourself and survive. To do that, you’ll need to gather resources, craft tools, hunt wild animals, catch fish, grow crops, and build a homestead that can sustain you while you try to figure out what happened to you.

As it turns out, the island you washed up on is one of 24 that make up an archipelago, and your adventure will take you to all of them, each of which has different environments, resources, and hidden treasures. So you’ll need to continuously upgrade your tools and figure out how to adapt to each island’s challenges.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/mayday-the-survival-island-screenshot-1787602371901.jpg

There aren’t any timed objectives or linear paths, so you decide the pace at which the story unfolds. If you want to spend hours building up your base, raising animals, and tending crops, you can do that. Or you can just find what you need to keep surviving and move on to the next part of the story, it’s up to you.

That story of Mayday: The Survival Island is focused on the mysteries of the island and how you ended up there. You’ll find strange symbols, magical totems, and fragments of a lost civilization that hint these islands are more than meets the eye. And the more you explore, the more you’ll question if ending up here was an accident and if escape is even possible. You can get a taste of all this with the free Steam demo .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/esports-manager-2026-key-art-1787602371901.png
